title: Forge Reporter/TokenMinter adapters — fix nominal-type mismatch with server/github
description:
[CIC-28](https://linear.app/cicadoci/issue/CIC-28/forge-adapter-interface-github-as-first-driver) shipped `forge.Reporter` and `forge.TokenMinter` with doc comments claiming `*github.ChecksClient` and `*github.InstallationTokenMinter` satisfy them "via structural typing." Go interface satisfaction is nominal, not structural: `forge.RunRef`/`RerunRef`/`Conclusion`/`Annotation` are distinct named types from their `github` package counterparts, so neither concrete type actually implements the corresponding `forge` interface. `TokenMinter.CloneCredentialsForRun` also has no `context.Context` parameter and no way to obtain an installation ID from a bare `RunRef`, so `*InstallationTokenMinter` doesn't match by signature either.

Flagged in review on [cicadoci/core#27](https://linear.app/cicadoci/review/cic-28-forge-adapter-interface-github-as-first-driver-2a0d8711bf74) ([CIC-28](https://linear.app/cicadoci/issue/CIC-28/forge-adapter-interface-github-as-first-driver)). Nothing in `server/main` wires `forge.NewGitHubForge` yet, so this is latent — it will fail to compile the moment real wiring is attempted.

Fix: add adapter types in `server/github` (which may depend on `server/forge`, a leaf package, without a cycle) that convert between the two type sets, add `ctx` to `TokenMinter.CloneCredentialsForRun`, and add an installation-ID resolver so the adapter can actually mint a token. Prove it with a compile-time assertion and tests.

title: Missing migration for `artifacts` table — server/artifacts.Postgres will fail at runtime
description:
## Finding

`server/artifacts/postgres.go`'s own doc comment says:

> Postgres is a Store backed by a SQL connection. It stores artifact metadata in the `artifacts` table (migration 0003).

But `server/store/migrations/` only contains `0001_init.sql` and `0002_widen_executor_check.sql`. There is no `artifacts` table anywhere in the schema. Every method on `artifacts.Postgres` (`Create`, `GetByRunID`, `GetByID`, `GetByRunAndName`, `Delete`, `FindExpired`) issues SQL directly against a table that does not exist, so the first real call will fail with `relation "artifacts" does not exist`.

This wasn't caught because `artifacts.Postgres` has zero test coverage — `server/artifacts/postgres_test.go` doesn't exist; only `memory_test.go` (against the `Memory` fake) does. CI's `test` job does run against a real Postgres service and fails the build if any DB-backed test is skipped, so a real test here would have caught this immediately — the gap is the missing test, not a CI weakness.

## Suggested fix

* Add `server/store/migrations/0003_artifacts.sql` creating the `artifacts` table matching the columns `Postgres.Create`/`selectCols` expect (id, org_id, run_id, job_id, name, blob_key, size_bytes, content_type, uploaded_at, expires_at, created_at).
* Add `server/artifacts/postgres_test.go` exercising `NewPostgres` against `CICADO_TEST_DATABASE_URL`, mirroring the pattern used by `server/queue/postgres_test.go` or `server/store/store_test.go`.

## Verified

* Confirmed via `grep` that no migration file defines `CREATE TABLE artifacts`, against both `0001_init.sql` and `0002_widen_executor_check.sql`.
* Confirmed `server/artifacts/postgres.go`'s own doc comment names a "migration 0003" that doesn't exist in the repo.
* Confirmed no test file references `artifacts.NewPostgres` anywhere in the tree.

## Unverified / needs follow-up

* Did not actually run `artifacts.Postgres` against a live Postgres to reproduce the failure (no wiring exists yet to invoke it — see [CIC-71](https://linear.app/cicadoci/issue/CIC-71/m3-m9-subsystems-are-built-but-never-wired-into-cmdcicado-server-most)) — this is inferred directly from the SQL referencing a nonexistent table, which is unambiguous, but a human should confirm with `go run` + a real DB before closing.

title: CIC-34 "Artifacts" ships no real presigned-URL implementation — only an in-memory fake exists
description:
## Finding

[CIC-34](https://linear.app/cicadoci/issue/CIC-34/artifacts-presigned-uploaddownload-namespacing-retention) ("Artifacts: presigned upload/download, namespacing, retention") is marked Done. The `artifacts.PreSignedURLProvider` interface exists (`UploadURL`/`DownloadURL`), but the only implementation anywhere in the tree is `artifacts.MemoryPreSigner` in `server/artifacts/memory.go`, which returns fake URLs for tests. There is no S3 (or any real object-store) implementation of `PreSignedURLProvider`.

This means the actual feature the ticket title promises — presigned upload/download against real storage — doesn't exist yet. What's been delivered is the interface, the metadata store (`Store`, `Memory`, and the currently-broken `Postgres` — see companion ticket), and a test fake. That's real, useful work, but it's not what "presigned upload/download" delivered means to a reader of the ticket or the project plan.

Related: `server/blobstore` (the interface artifacts are meant to sit on top of for the actual bytes) also has no S3 driver — only `blobstore.Memory`.

## Suggested fix

Add a real S3-backed `PreSignedURLProvider` (wrapping `s3.PresignClient` from aws-sdk-go-v2) and a real S3-backed `blobstore.BlobStore`, or explicitly re-scope [CIC-34](https://linear.app/cicadoci/issue/CIC-34/artifacts-presigned-uploaddownload-namespacing-retention)/re-open it to track "S3 driver" as remaining work rather than leaving it silently implied as done.

## Verified

* Grepped the whole tree for implementations of `PreSignedURLProvider`; only `MemoryPreSigner` exists.
* Grepped for any S3 client usage (`s3.NewFromConfig`, `PresignClient`, etc.) in `server/artifacts/` and `server/blobstore/`; none found.

## Unverified / needs follow-up

* Whether this is intentionally deferred to M9 packaging/hardening rather than M4 — if so, the ticket description or plan should say so explicitly rather than reading as delivered.

title: Redaction masker never learns a real secret value in production — RegisterWithVariants is dead code outside its own tests
description:
## Finding

CLAUDE.md's security invariants state: "Secret redaction runs on log ingest, before persistence or fan-out." `server/redact.RegisteredMasker.RegisterWithVariants(raw)` is the *only* mechanism by which a masker ever learns a real secret value to scrub (it also registers base64/URL-encoded variants). Grepping the whole tree, `RegisterWithVariants` is called nowhere except inside `server/redact/masker_test.go`.

Two concrete places that mint or hold real secret-shaped values never register them:

1. `server/github.CloneCredentialsForRunOnClient` (server/github/installation.go) mints a real, short-lived GitHub installation access token and embeds it directly in a git clone URL. This has been a known, explicitly-documented gap since [CIC-26](https://linear.app/cicadoci/issue/CIC-26/per-job-github-installation-tokens-for-clone-never-persisted)'s review (PR [cicadoci/core#25](https://linear.app/cicadoci/review/cic-26-per-job-github-installation-tokens-for-clone-ff5aad07bd3f)) and again at [CIC-31](https://linear.app/cicadoci/issue/CIC-31/secret-redaction-on-log-ingest-adversarial-test-suite) (PR [cicadoci/core#30](https://linear.app/cicadoci/review/cic-31-secret-redaction-on-log-ingest-adversarial-test-suite-6c58e39a0f0d)) — both decision-log entries say registration "is documented but not yet wired" — but across two more milestones of work it still hasn't been closed.
2. Even setting aside (1): as noted in the companion ticket ([CIC-71](https://linear.app/cicadoci/issue/CIC-71/m3-m9-subsystems-are-built-but-never-wired-into-cmdcicado-server-most)), `main.go`'s `runnersvc.DefaultConfig()` explicitly sets `Masker: redact.NoopMasker{}`, so even if something did call `RegisterWithVariants`, the production `Service` isn't using a `RegisteredMasker` at all — it's using the no-op.

Net effect: today, if a job's log output or error text ever contained a real installation token (e.g., a failed `git clone` printing the URL with credentials, which is a very ordinary git failure mode), it would NOT be redacted. This directly contradicts the security invariant above and the MVP's [cicadoci/core#1](https://linear.app/cicadoci/review/cic-9-repo-hygiene-docs-restructure-and-pr-conventions-ffddbcbfe4ab) non-negotiable success criterion: "A secret set in the UI never appears in any log (verified by adversarial test suite)." The adversarial test suite ([CIC-31](https://linear.app/cicadoci/issue/CIC-31/secret-redaction-on-log-ingest-adversarial-test-suite), excellent as far as it goes) only proves the masker redacts values it's been told about — it doesn't prove any real value ever gets told to it.

## Suggested fix

* Wire `CloneCredentialsForRunOnClient` (or its caller, once the forge/webhook path is wired per [CIC-71](https://linear.app/cicadoci/issue/CIC-71/m3-m9-subsystems-are-built-but-never-wired-into-cmdcicado-server-most)) to call `masker.RegisterWithVariants(token)` immediately after minting, before the token is used in any command that could be logged.
* Wire a real `*redact.RegisteredMasker` into `runnersvc.Config.Masker` in `main.go` instead of `NoopMasker{}`.
* Add an integration-level adversarial test that goes through the real minting + masking path end-to-end (not just the masker in isolation), so this can't silently regress again.

## Verified

* `grep -rn "RegisterWithVariants"` across the whole tree: only `server/redact/masker.go` (definition) and `server/redact/masker_test.go` (3 call sites, all in tests).
* Read `server/github/installation.go` and confirmed `CloneCredentialsForRunOnClient` has no masker parameter or call.
* Read `server/runnersvc/service.go`'s `DefaultConfig()` and confirmed `Masker: redact.NoopMasker{}`.
* Read the [CIC-26](https://linear.app/cicadoci/issue/CIC-26/per-job-github-installation-tokens-for-clone-never-persisted) and [CIC-31](https://linear.app/cicadoci/issue/CIC-31/secret-redaction-on-log-ingest-adversarial-test-suite) decision-log entries in CLAUDE.md, both of which independently flag this exact gap as known-but-not-closed.

## Unverified / needs follow-up

* Whether there's a different, not-yet-built call site (e.g., inside the not-yet-wired webhook dispatcher) that's meant to own this instead of `CloneCredentialsForRunOnClient` directly — worth deciding as part of the fix rather than assuming.

title: CIC-55 "MCP server" has no actual MCP protocol transport — unreachable by any real MCP client
description:
## Finding

[CIC-55](https://linear.app/cicadoci/issue/CIC-55/mcp-server-read-only-diagnostic-tools) ("MCP server: read-only diagnostic tools") is marked Done. `server/mcp/server.go`'s own package doc is explicit about scope:

> In this MVP seed, it exposes the tool definitions and the dispatch mechanism as plain Go methods. The JSON-RPC transport and MCP protocol wiring come in a follow-up ticket.

So `Server.ListRuns`/`GetRun`/`ClassifyFailure`/etc. are ordinary Go methods on a struct — there is no `stdio`, HTTP+SSE, or streamable-HTTP MCP transport anywhere in the tree, and (per [CIC-71](https://linear.app/cicadoci/issue/CIC-71/m3-m9-subsystems-are-built-but-never-wired-into-cmdcicado-server-most)) it isn't constructed by `main.go` regardless. No real MCP client — Claude Desktop, Claude Code, or any other agent — can connect to this today.

This matters because it's the literal M8 exit criterion in the project plan: "the success-criteria Claude eval passes ≥8/10" (§3: "Claude, pointed at the MCP server, can correctly explain why a seeded failing build failed"). That eval requires an actual MCP endpoint to point Claude at. `server/ai`'s eval harness ([CIC-57](https://linear.app/cicadoci/issue/CIC-57/ai-triage-eval-harness-10-seeded-failure-scenarios-810-gate), Done) calls `classify.Classify` directly in-process — it's a genuinely good baseline-accuracy measurement for the rule-based classifier, but it is not, and can't yet be, the "point Claude at the MCP server" eval the plan describes, since there's no server to point at.

## Suggested fix

* Add a real MCP transport (the reference Go SDK's `stdio` or streamable-HTTP transport is the natural fit) that exposes `Server`'s methods as MCP tools per the MCP spec's tool schema.
* Wire it into `main.go` per [CIC-71](https://linear.app/cicadoci/issue/CIC-71/m3-m9-subsystems-are-built-but-never-wired-into-cmdcicado-server-most), gated by `mcpauth.Authorizer`.
* Once reachable, run the actual "point Claude at it" eval described in the plan's success criteria, distinct from the in-process classifier-accuracy eval [CIC-57](https://linear.app/cicadoci/issue/CIC-57/ai-triage-eval-harness-10-seeded-failure-scenarios-810-gate) already covers.

## Verified

* Read `server/mcp/server.go`'s package doc, which self-documents the transport gap.
* Grepped the tree for any MCP transport/SDK usage (`mcp.NewServer`, `stdio`, JSON-RPC framing) tied to `server/mcp`; none found.
* Confirmed (per [CIC-71](https://linear.app/cicadoci/issue/CIC-71/m3-m9-subsystems-are-built-but-never-wired-into-cmdcicado-server-most)) `server/mcp` is not constructed anywhere in `main.go`.

## Unverified / needs follow-up

* Which MCP transport (stdio vs. HTTP) fits the deployment model best — self-hosted server implies HTTP-based is likely right, but that's a product decision, not inferred here.

title: CIC-41 "Audit event pipeline" — nothing in the codebase ever calls Append; zero audit events are written
description:
## Finding

[CIC-41](https://linear.app/cicadoci/issue/CIC-41/audit-event-pipeline-all-surfaces-one-chokepoint) ("Audit event pipeline (all surfaces, one chokepoint)") is marked Done. `server/audit/audit.go` implements a solid `Log` interface with an in-memory hash-chained implementation (`MemoryLog`) and a well-designed `Action` taxonomy (`ActionApprove`, `ActionCancel`, `ActionRerun`, `ActionDeploy`, `ActionRollback`, `ActionSecretPut`, `ActionSecretDelete`) — the package itself is good work with solid test coverage.

But grepping the whole tree for any caller of `audit.` outside `server/audit/` itself turns up nothing except an unrelated doc-comment mention in `server/workflow/types.go`. No surface — not the approval-gates handler, not the secrets store's `Put`/`Delete`, not the webhook-triggered run creation (once that's wired), not the MCP tool-invocation audit (which uses its own separate, unrelated `mcpauth.AuditEntry`/`MemoryAuditor` mechanism, not this package) — ever calls `Append`. There is also no Postgres-backed `Log` implementation; only `MemoryLog` exists, so even once wired, nothing would survive a restart yet.

This directly contradicts CLAUDE.md's stated invariant: "Every state-changing action from any surface (web/chat/MCP/API) writes an audit event," and the ticket's own "all surfaces, one chokepoint" framing. Today there is a well-built chokepoint that zero surfaces flow through.

## Suggested fix

* Wire `audit.Append` calls into the real state-changing call sites as each surface gets wired per [CIC-71](https://linear.app/cicadoci/issue/CIC-71/m3-m9-subsystems-are-built-but-never-wired-into-cmdcicado-server-most): `approvalgates.Manager.Resolve` (approve/deny), `secrets.Store.Put`/`Delete`, run cancel/rerun handlers, deploy-job dispatch.
* Add a Postgres-backed `audit.Log` implementation against the existing `audit_events` table (which already exists in `0001_init.sql` — the schema is ready, just unused by this package).
* Consider consolidating with `mcpauth`'s separate audit mechanism so there's genuinely one chokepoint rather than two parallel ones.

## Verified

* `grep -rln "audit\."` across the whole tree outside `server/audit/`: only one hit, a doc comment in `server/workflow/types.go`, not a call.
* Confirmed no Postgres-backed implementation of `audit.Log` exists (only `MemoryLog`).
* Confirmed the `audit_events` table already exists in `server/store/migrations/0001_init.sql`, so schema is not the blocker.
* Confirmed `server/mcpauth` has its own separate, unrelated audit mechanism (`AuditEntry`/`MemoryAuditor`) that doesn't use `server/audit` at all.

## Unverified / needs follow-up

* Whether consolidating the two audit mechanisms is in scope now or should be tracked separately — flagging the duplication for a human decision rather than assuming.

title: Per-PR knowledge-graph currency — keep the /understand graph in lockstep with master
description:
## Context

The repo now carries an `/understand` knowledge graph at `.ua/knowledge-graph.json`
(a `.ua/fingerprints.json` delta baseline + `.ua/meta.json` provenance). If that graph is
not kept in lockstep with the tip of `master`, every downstream consumer — agent context,
`/understand-diff`, the knowledge-graph dashboard — silently reasons about a *past* revision
of the code, and the per-PR diff overlay becomes misleading.

This ticket introduces a standing convention (owner-directed, parallel to the per-PR
decision-log policy of CIC-103) and commits the first knowledge snapshot.

## What lands

1. **First knowledge snapshot** — `.ua/knowledge-graph.json`, `.ua/fingerprints.json`,
   `.ua/meta.json` (+ `.ua/config.json`, `.ua/.understandignore`). Scratch
   (`.ua/.trash-*/`, `.ua/intermediate/`) and the transient `.ua/diff-overlay.json` are git-ignored.
2. **Currency convention**, recorded three ways so it survives drift:
   * `CLAUDE.md` → new "Knowledge graph currency" section + a per-PR Verified-checklist line.
   * `docs/decisions/CIC-104-knowledge-graph-currency.md` — the dated decision record.
   * `docs/decisions/README.md` — new "Process conventions (owner-directed)" section registering it.
   * `.gitignore` — keep the 5 artifacts tracked, ignore the scratch.

## The two-skill split

* `/understand-diff` **— *determine the change*.** Maps changed files → graph nodes, finds
  1-hop affected components / touched layers, scores risk, writes `.ua/diff-overlay.json`, and
  *warns* when the graph is stale (committed/working-tree diff since `meta.json.gitCommitHash`
  is non-empty). Run when opening or rebasing a stacked PR.
* `/understand` **— *refresh the graph*.** Incremental: with the baseline present it
  re-scans/re-extracts only changed files, reassembles, validates, and rewrites all three
  artifacts. No LLM subagents needed for a normal refresh. Run before a PR lands on `master`,
  and commit the refreshed `.ua/` artifacts.

**Staleness signal:** the graph is current when `git diff --name-only <graphCommit>..HEAD -- .` (project-scoped) is empty. `/understand-diff` prints the warning
automatically — treat it as a "refresh" signal, never a reason to skip the diff.

## Verified

* `/understand` was run deterministically (no LLM subagents in this env): scan → 13 batches →
  extract → `GraphBuilder` → merge (1,685 nodes / 2,487 edges) → 10 curated layers + 10-step
  architectural tour → validate → save. `validateGraph` + `validateForWriting` return 0 errors.
* `git check-ignore` confirms the 5 artifacts are tracked and `intermediate/`, `.trash-*/`,
  `diff-overlay.json` are ignored.
* `meta.json` records the generation commit + `lastAnalyzedAt` and the analyzed-file count.

## Unverified / needs follow-up

* `meta.json.gitCommitHash` is the 71h stack tip (`5e4fc27`), not `master`, because the
  decision-log infrastructure this sits on is not yet on `master`. The graph should be
  refreshed (`/understand`) onto each new `master` tip as the 71x stack lands — this is the
  first real use of the convention itself, and a live staleness warning will surface it.
* The owner makes the merge decision (no self-merge).

title: Production server creates runs but never jobs: WorkflowLoader is nil and nothing writes the workflows table
description:
Found in a QC audit of `master` @ `c8d89fc` (2026-09-30).

## What's wrong

Every push or PR webhook creates a `runs` row, and then nothing happens. No job is ever created, so no job is dispatched to a runner.

* `server/cmd/cicado-server/main.go:157` builds the controller with `controller.DefaultConfig().WithAudit(auditLog)`. `DefaultConfig()` leaves `WorkflowLoader` nil (`server/controller/controller.go:83`), and a nil loader is documented as "a silent no-op" (`controller.go:15`).
* `controller.NewStoreLoader` (CIC-71e, `server/controller/jobs.go:115`) is called only from tests.
* Even once it is wired, nothing in the codebase ever writes the `workflows` table. `StoreLoader` would return zero workflows.

## Impact

The core product loop (webhook → run → jobs → runner) is broken in the shipped binary. Runs stay queued with zero jobs. [CIC-71](https://linear.app/cicadoci/issue/CIC-71/m3-m9-subsystems-are-built-but-never-wired-into-cmdcicado-server-most) lists 71a–71h as landed, which gives the impression the loop is live.

## Fix

1. Wire a loader in `main.go`, e.g. `DefaultConfig().WithAudit(a).WithWorkflowLoader(controller.NewStoreLoader(st, log))`. Add the builder if it doesn't exist.
2. Add the write path that fills `workflows`: a GitHub loader that fetches `.cicado/*.yml` at the head SHA, or a sync on push. Its output must use the JSON shape `StoreLoader.LoadAll` decodes (the [cicadoci/core#79](https://linear.app/cicadoci/review/cic-71e-storeloader-reads-workflow-definitions-from-db-3aa14e4960b1) review asked for a shared contract).
3. Decide what a run with zero matching workflows should do: complete it as `skipped`/`success` rather than leave it queued forever.
4. Add a test proving `main`'s config has a non-nil loader. At minimum, `DefaultConfig` should document that `main` must set one.

## Acceptance

With `-dev-seed` (or a seeded `workflows` row), a signed push webhook creates jobs that a runner claims.

title: Webhook signature verification is silently disabled when CICADO_WEBHOOK_SECRET is unset
description:
Found in a QC audit of `master` @ `c8d89fc` (2026-09-30). Security.

## What's wrong

* `server/cmd/cicado-server/main.go:61`: `-webhook-secret` defaults to `$CICADO_WEBHOOK_SECRET`, with help text "empty disables verification".
* `server/webhook/receiver.go:112`: `if r.secret != "" { Verify(...) }`. With no secret, **every** POST to `/api/v1/webhooks/github` is accepted unsigned.
* The server starts with no warning and no opt-in. Compare the secrets key right next to it, which refuses to start unless `-allow-ephemeral-key` is passed explicitly (`main.go:64`, `:130`).

## Impact

A deployment that forgets the environment variable accepts forged webhooks from anyone who can reach the HTTP port. Once jobs are wired (see the loader ticket), a forged push or PR event can trigger runs for any installed repo and branch. This fails open on an internet-facing endpoint, against the CLAUDE.md security invariants.

## Fix

Fail closed, mirroring the ephemeral-key pattern:

1. If the webhook secret is empty, refuse to start unless an explicit dev flag is set (e.g. `-allow-unsigned-webhooks` / `CICADO_ALLOW_UNSIGNED_WEBHOOKS=true`).
2. When that flag is set, log `Warn` at startup and on each unsigned delivery.
3. Update the flag help text, `docs/development.md` and docker-compose (local dev sets the dev flag).
4. Test: the server refuses to start with an empty secret and no flag, and the receiver rejects unsigned requests when a secret is configured (already covered).

## Acceptance

`cicado-server` with no webhook secret and no dev flag exits with a clear error.

title: Production workflow producer: fetch .cicado workflow files at the event SHA and UpsertWorkflow them
description:
Split out of [CIC-78](https://linear.app/cicadoci/issue/CIC-78/production-server-creates-runs-but-never-jobs-workflowloader-is-nil) (PR [cicadoci/core#89](https://linear.app/cicadoci/review/cic-78-wire-store-backed-workflow-loader-add-upsertworkflow-fix-nil-9d8a21a804ae)), deferred by the orchestrator (ref c6e323): this must land before [CIC-82](https://linear.app/cicadoci/issue/CIC-82/built-but-unwired-subsystems-in-cicado-server-live-log-sse)/83.

## What's missing

[CIC-78](https://linear.app/cicadoci/issue/CIC-78/production-server-creates-runs-but-never-jobs-workflowloader-is-nil) wires `StoreLoader` into `cicado-server` and adds `Store.UpsertWorkflow`. Outside `-dev-seed`, though, nothing writes the `workflows` table, so a production server still creates runs and never jobs.

## Fix

* On a push or PR webhook, fetch the repo's workflow files at the head SHA through the GitHub App installation token, parse them with `controller.ParseWorkflowBytes`, and store each one with `UpsertWorkflow`. The stored `Definition` must be the JSON shape `StoreLoader.LoadAll` decodes.
* Decide where the fetch runs: in the controller before `LoadAndCreateJobs`, or as a sync step. Then decide how parse errors are reported (log a warning; later, a failed check).
* Optional: revision-pinned loading. `StoreLoader` ignores its `sha` argument today.

## Acceptance

On a real (non-dev-seed) server, a signed push webhook for an installed repo that has a workflow file creates jobs that a runner claims.

title: Step `if: failure | always` (CIC-22) never reaches the runner: no wire field, runner stops at first failed step
description:
Found in QC of `master` @ `5d6722f` (2026-10-01).

## What's wrong

The parser and validator accept step `if: success|failure|always` (`server/workflow/parse/parse.go:500`, `validate.go:129`), but:

* `StepSpec` in the runner proto (fields 1–7) has no condition field.
* `runner/job.go:163` returns on the first failing step. A cleanup step marked `if: always` or `if: failure` never runs.

The feature is documented as merged ([CIC-22](https://linear.app/cicadoci/issue/CIC-22/trigger-filters-branchtag-if-step-status-conditionals), PR [cicadoci/core#20](https://linear.app/cicadoci/review/cic-22-trigger-filters-if-conditionals-26b7e059da85)) but has no runtime effect. Workflows that rely on cleanup or notify-on-failure steps silently skip them.

## Fix

1. Add `string if = 8` (enum preferred) to `StepSpec`. This is an additive proto change, so `make proto-breaking` stays green.
2. Persist it in `steps` (new column plus migration) and send it in the assignment.
3. In the runner, track job outcome and run steps per their condition after a failure. The job result stays failed.

## Acceptance

Runner unit test: steps \[fail, `if: always`, `if: success`\]. Steps 1 and 2 execute, step 3 is skipped, and the job ends failed.

title: Secrets can never reach a job: secret_refs is never populated and the runner never calls GetJobSecrets
description:
Found in a QC audit of `master` @ `c8d89fc` (2026-09-30).

## What's wrong

The `GetJobSecrets` RPC ([CIC-38](https://linear.app/cicadoci/issue/CIC-38/getjobsecrets-rpc-lease-authorized-delivery-memory-only-on-runner)) and the masker registration ([CIC-74](https://linear.app/cicadoci/issue/CIC-74/redaction-masker-never-learns-a-real-secret-value-in-production)) are correct in isolation, but nothing on either side reaches them:

* **Server:** `controller.secretRefsFor` (`server/controller/jobs.go:219`) always returns `nil` (`TODO(CIC-38/39/40)`). Every job therefore has an empty `secret_refs`, and `GetJobSecrets` returns an empty map early (`server/runnersvc/service.go`, `len(secretRefs) == 0`).
* **Runner:** nothing under `runner/` calls `GetJobSecrets`. `runner/executor/docker.go:63` says it "is not wired".
* **Workflow schema:** there is no way to declare secret references. `server/workflow/types.go:258-259` claims "Secret references (e.g. `secrets.DEPLOY_ROLE`) are resolved by the runner at step start via GetJobSecrets", which is false today. A `secrets.X` value in `env:` reaches the step as the literal string.

## Impact

The M5 exit criterion ("a deploy job assumes an AWS role … zero stored AWS keys") and any workflow that needs a secret cannot work. The docs and code comments say it does.

## Fix

1. Define how a workflow references secrets (e.g. parse `secrets.NAME` in job/step `env`, or add an explicit `secrets:` list). Validate it in `server/workflow/validate.go`.
2. Implement `secretRefsFor` from that definition, with names only.
3. Runner: call `GetJobSecrets` with the lease after claiming a job, substitute values into the step env in memory only, and never write them to logs or the journal.
4. The service-wide masker (`service.go:335`) keeps every delivered secret forever. Consider scoping registration per job, or document the growth bound.
5. Add an end-to-end test: a workflow using `secrets.FOO` gets the value in its env, and the value is masked in stored logs.
6. Fix the `types.go` comment until this lands.

## Acceptance

A job whose env references a stored secret receives the value, and the value is redacted from `log_entries`.

title: pull_request webhook decodes the wrong JSON shape: fork flag is always false (fork-PR policy bypassed), base ref and head SHA always empty
description:
Found in QC of `master` @ `5d6722f` (2026-10-01).

## What's wrong

`webhook.PullRequestPayload` (`server/webhook/events.go:42`) reads `base`, `head` and `fork` from the top level of the event. GitHub nests them: `pull_request.base.ref`, `pull_request.head.sha`, `pull_request.head.ref`, `pull_request.head.repo.full_name`, and the fork signal is `pull_request.head.repo.fork` (or head repo ≠ base repo). There is no top-level `fork` field.

The tests pass only because the fixtures in `server/webhook/receiver_test.go:431` and `:525` use the same invented flat shape.

## Impact on a real GitHub delivery

* `payload.Fork` is always `false`, so `runs.is_fork` is always false.
  * `controller.LoadAndCreateJobs` never applies `ForkPolicy` (`server/controller/jobs.go:287`).
  * `GetJobSecrets` fork guard (`server/runnersvc/service.go:302`) never fires. Once [CIC-79](https://linear.app/cicadoci/issue/CIC-79/secrets-can-never-reach-a-job-secret-refs-is-never-populated-and-the) lands, a fork PR would receive repo secrets. **Security invariant break.**
* `Base.Ref` is empty, so the run's ref is `""` and `branches:` trigger filters never match.
* `Head.SHA` is empty, so runs and forge reports carry no commit SHA.

## Fix

1. Model the real payload: `PullRequest struct { Base{Ref, Repo}, Head{Ref, SHA, Repo{FullName, Fork}} } \`json:"pull_request"\``, plus `sender.login\`.
2. Compute fork as `head.repo.fork || head.repo.full_name != repository.full_name`. Treat a null `head.repo` (deleted fork) as a fork.
3. Replace the hand-written fixtures with a trimmed real GitHub `pull_request` payload under `testdata/`. Assert fork=true end to end through to `runs.is_fork`.

## Acceptance

A recorded GitHub fork-PR payload produces a run with `is_fork = true`, non-empty ref and SHA, and the fork policy is applied.

title: Regression from CIC-79 (#91): every job fails as infra, because the runner calls GetJobSecrets without its credential (Unauthenticated)
description:
Found on `master` @ `f445f0d` (2026-10-02). Reported by Dwight; confirmed by Creed.

## Symptom

`./scripts/with-postgres.sh go test -race -count=1 ./test/e2e/...` fails 5 tests: `TestWalkingSkeleton`, `TestFailingStepIsReportedWithExitCode`, `TestCancelPropagates`, `TestRunnerSurvivesServerRestart` and `TestSweepRequeuesExpiredJob`. All passed at `0034d5d`. The only code commit since then is `f445f0d` ([CIC-79](https://linear.app/cicadoci/issue/CIC-79/secrets-can-never-reach-a-job-secret-refs-is-never-populated-and-the), PR [cicadoci/core#91](https://linear.app/cicadoci/review/cic-79-deliver-secrets-to-a-job-end-to-end-high-fc8879db8015)).

Every job ends `failed`, exit -1, `error_class=infra`, and the runner logs:

```
fetch job secrets ... error="runner: get job secrets: rpc error: code = Unauthenticated desc = missing credentials"
```

## Cause

`runner/job.go:143` calls `fetchJobSecrets(ctx, a.secrets, jobID, leaseID)` with the job context. The unary `GetJobSecrets` RPC needs the runner bearer token in the `authorization` metadata (`server/runnersvc/service.go:345` `authenticate`). The agent attaches it only through `a.authContext(ctx)` (`runner/agent.go:179`), and this call skips that. Unit tests use a fake `secretsClient`, so they never cross the real interceptor or auth path.

This is a production break as well as a test failure: every job on a real runner fails before its first step, **including jobs that reference no secrets**, because the fetch is unconditional.

## Fix

1. Call `fetchJobSecrets(a.authContext(ctx), ...)` (or attach the credential inside `fetchJobSecrets`).
2. Skip the RPC when the assignment carries no secret refs, so a secrets-service outage can't fail jobs that don't need secrets.
3. Add an e2e test that a job with a `secrets.X` env ref receives the value, through the real runner and server.

## Acceptance

The 5 e2e tests pass on master again. A new e2e test proves end-to-end secret delivery.

title: OIDC job token `sub` is `job:<run>:<job>`: AWS trust policies cannot scope roles to repo/branch/env (contradicts architecture)
description:
Found in QC of `master` @ `0034d5d` (2026-10-01). Security design bug in [CIC-39](https://linear.app/cicadoci/issue/CIC-39/oidc-issuer-job-identity-tokens-jwks-endpoint) (`server/oidc`). It is not wired yet, so fix it before wiring.

## What's wrong

* The issuer's subject is `job:<run-uuid>:<job-name>` (`SubjectFor` / `parseSubject`, `server/oidc/issuer.go`; `docs/decisions/CIC-39-oidc-issuer.md:50`). Repo, branch and environment are only in custom claims (`repo`, `branch`, `sha`).
* For a generic (non-GitHub) OIDC provider, AWS IAM trust policies can only condition on `aud`, `sub` and `amr`. Custom claims such as `repo`/`branch` are **not** usable in a trust policy.
* So a role that trusts the CICaDo issuer can only say "any job from this CICaDo server", or pin one random run UUID, which is useless. Any job on the instance, from any repo or org (and, if the fork policy fails, a fork PR), could assume every role that trusts the issuer.
* `project-docs/02-architecture.md:106` specifies: *trust conditions on* `sub` *= org/repo/branch/env,* `aud`. The implementation contradicts it.

## Fix

* Make `sub` encode the trust-relevant tuple in a fixed order, with escaping. For example `repo:<org>/<repo>:ref:refs/heads/<branch>:env:<env>` (GitHub's convention, which users already know how to write `StringLike` conditions for). Fork PRs get a distinct form such as `repo:<org>/<repo>:pull_request`, so no branch- or env-scoped role ever matches a fork.
* Keep run/job in custom claims (and `jti`) for audit.
* Update the decision doc and the planned Terraform trust-policy example.

## Acceptance

Tests show tokens for different repos, branches, or fork vs non-fork runs get subjects that a `StringLike` condition such as `repo:acme/api:ref:refs/heads/main:*` can tell apart.

title: Job graph never advances and run status never changes: `needs` dependents stay pending forever, runs never finish
description:
Found in QC of `master` @ `5d6722f` (2026-10-01).

## What's wrong

* `store.CreateJobSpecs` (`server/store/runs.go:156`) queues only the top-level jobs. Jobs with `needs` stay `pending`.
* No code anywhere promotes a `pending` job to `queued` when its dependencies succeed. `queue.Complete` (`server/queue/postgres.go`) only updates the finished job, and no database trigger does it either (checked `0001_init.sql` to `0003`). The only other `Enqueue` caller is `devseed.go`.
* No code marks dependents `skipped`/`cancelled` when a dependency fails or dead-letters.
* No code ever updates `runs.status`. It stays `pending` from `CreateRun` onward, whatever the jobs do.

So any workflow using `needs` ([CIC-21](https://linear.app/cicadoci/issue/CIC-21/dag-resolution-needs-fan-outfan-in-scheduling) fan-out/fan-in) runs only its first wave and then hangs. Every run looks pending forever in the API, and to the forge once [CIC-81](https://linear.app/cicadoci/issue/CIC-81/server-never-reports-check-status-to-github-and-re-run-does-nothing) lands.

Related: [CIC-85](https://linear.app/cicadoci/issue/CIC-85/runs-with-zero-matching-workflows-stay-queued-forever-finalise-them-as) covers runs with zero workflows only. [CIC-78](https://linear.app/cicadoci/issue/CIC-78/production-server-creates-runs-but-never-jobs-workflowloader-is-nil) covers job creation.

## Fix

In the same transaction as `queue.Complete` (and `Requeue` when it dead-letters):

1. Queue each dependent whose dependencies have all succeeded, honouring the `if: always` fan-in rule in `workflow/dag.go:248`.
2. Skip or cancel dependents of a failed job.
3. Roll up run status: running on first claim, then succeeded / failed / cancelled when all jobs are terminal.

Add an e2e test: a 3-job diamond DAG runs to completion and the run ends `succeeded`.

Also: `store.CompleteJob` (`runs.go:250`) has no callers and writes a terminal status without a lease check. Delete it or make it lease-checked.

title: Webhook-created jobs carry no steps and no git checkout info: convertJobSpecs drops Steps, GitCloneURL, GitRef, GitSha
description:
Found in QC of `master` @ `5d6722f` (2026-10-01).

## What's wrong

`controller.convertJobSpecs` (`server/controller/jobs.go:167`) builds `store.JobSpec` from a workflow job, but:

* `store.JobSpec` has no `Steps` field, and nothing writes the `steps` table except `devseed.go:126`. A job created from a workflow has zero steps. The runner claims it, runs nothing, and reports success.
* `GitCloneURL`, `GitRef` and `GitSha` are never set, so the runner's `GitContext` is empty and there is no checkout.
* `Executor` is hard-coded to `"cicanscript"` whatever the workflow says.

This is separate from [CIC-78](https://linear.app/cicadoci/issue/CIC-78/production-server-creates-runs-but-never-jobs-workflowloader-is-nil) (loader nil, workflows table empty). Even with [CIC-78](https://linear.app/cicadoci/issue/CIC-78/production-server-creates-runs-but-never-jobs-workflowloader-is-nil) / PR [cicadoci/core#89](https://linear.app/cicadoci/review/cic-78-wire-store-backed-workflow-loader-add-upsertworkflow-fix-nil-9d8a21a804ae) merged, jobs will run nothing unless that PR also persists steps. Please check [cicadoci/core#89](https://linear.app/cicadoci/review/cic-78-wire-store-backed-workflow-loader-add-upsertworkflow-fix-nil-9d8a21a804ae) before starting.

## Fix

1. Add `Steps []StepSpec` to `store.JobSpec` and insert into `steps` inside the `CreateJobSpecs` transaction: index, name, command/run, env, timeout, image. Also carry the step `if:` value (see the step `if:` ticket).
2. Pass the clone URL, ref and SHA from the controller (head repo/SHA for PRs) into each spec.
3. Map the executor from the workflow (container image → docker), not a constant.

## Acceptance

A push webhook for a seeded 2-step workflow produces a claimed job whose `JobAssignment` has both steps and a populated `GitContext`.

title: Webhook events are silently lost: delivery marked "seen" before dispatch, and controller errors/backpressure return 200
description:
Found in QC of `master` @ `5d6722f` (2026-10-01).

## What's wrong

1. **Dedup before success.** `Receiver.ServeHTTP` (`server/webhook/receiver.go:154`) records `X-GitHub-Delivery` as seen *before* dispatching. If dispatch then fails (500), the operator's "Redeliver" in GitHub reuses the same delivery GUID and gets `200 duplicate`. The event can never be processed.
2. **Errors swallowed as success.** `Controller.HandlePush` / `HandlePullRequest` return `nil` when `resolveRepo` fails (`server/controller/controller.go:139`, `:215`), e.g. a transient database error. GitHub gets 200, so no run is created and there is no signal to retry.
3. **Backpressure drops with 200.** When `Backpressure.Acquire` says no, the handler returns `nil`, so the push or PR is discarded and GitHub sees success.
4. **Misleading comments.** `receiver.go:97` and `:177` say GitHub "will retry" a 503/501. GitHub does not automatically retry failed webhook deliveries; only manual or API redelivery exists.

## Fix

* Mark the delivery seen only after a successful dispatch, or remove the entry on failure.
* Return an error (→ 5xx) from the controller for transient store failures.
* Either queue over-limit events (preferred: create the run, and let the dispatcher enforce concurrency) or return 503 rather than 200.
* Correct the comments. Consider a redelivery sweep using GitHub's "list deliveries" API for failed ones.

## Acceptance

Tests: a failed dispatch followed by redelivery with the same GUID is processed. A store error yields 5xx.

title: Cleanup: stale/misattributed TODOs and code comments, abandoned runner/lambda stub
description:
Found in a QC audit of `master` @ `c8d89fc` (2026-09-30). Low risk, but these comments currently mislead readers and agents.

* `server/runnersvc/logstream.go:317`: `TODO(CIC-37): masker scrubs against an empty registered-value set` is stale. `GetJobSecrets` feeds the masker at `service.go:335` ([CIC-74](https://linear.app/cicadoci/issue/CIC-74/redaction-masker-never-learns-a-real-secret-value-in-production), Done). Remove it, or point it at the secrets-delivery ticket.
* `server/controller/controller.go:267`, `:279`: `TODO(CIC-71d)` refers to a merged ticket. Point them at the forge/rerequest ticket.

title: Runs with zero matching workflows stay queued forever: finalise them as skipped
description:
Split out of [CIC-78](https://linear.app/cicadoci/issue/CIC-78/production-server-creates-runs-but-never-jobs-workflowloader-is-nil) fix item 3 (PR [cicadoci/core#89](https://linear.app/cicadoci/review/cic-78-wire-store-backed-workflow-loader-add-upsertworkflow-fix-nil-9d8a21a804ae)), deferred by the orchestrator (ref c6e323).

## What's wrong

`controller.LoadAndCreateJobs` returns nil on both zero-job paths, so the run row stays queued/pending forever:

* `server/controller/jobs.go:263`: the repo has no workflows.
* `server/controller/jobs.go:330`: no workflow matched the event.

Until the production workflow producer lands, this is every production webhook. Once [CIC-81](https://linear.app/cicadoci/issue/CIC-81/server-never-reports-check-status-to-github-and-re-run-does-nothing) reports checks, these runs would also leave a GitHub check pending forever.

## Fix

When `created == 0`, move the run to a terminal state (`skipped`, or `success` with a reason), write an audit event, and, once a real forge exists, complete the check as neutral or skipped. Test both zero-job paths.

## Acceptance

A webhook for a repo with no matching workflow produces a run in a terminal state, not one left queued.

title: Backpressure in controller limits concurrent webhook handlers, not concurrent runs (slot released when the HTTP handler returns)
description:
Found in QC of `master` @ `5d6722f` (2026-10-01).

## What's wrong

`HandlePush` and `HandlePullRequest` (`server/controller/controller.go:145-153`, `:221-229`) call `Backpressure.Acquire` and `defer Release` in the same function. The slot is held only for the few milliseconds of run creation, then released, while the run and its jobs execute for minutes.

The result is that the per-repo/per-org limit almost never trips, and the runs it is meant to bound are unlimited. When it does trip, the event is dropped (see the "webhook events are silently lost" ticket).

Correction (2026-10-01, from Oscar's review): `server/dispatch` *does* support a tracker (`dispatch.Config.Backpressure`, `server/dispatch/dispatcher.go:55`, enforced around `:276`). But `main.go` builds the dispatcher with `dispatch.DefaultConfig(...)` and leaves it nil, so in the shipped binary only the controller-side tracker is active. The fix is to set the dispatch-side tracker in `main.go`, and to remove or keep only the controller-side acquire.

## Fix

Move enforcement to dispatch/claim: count `claimed`/`running` jobs per repo/org, or acquire at claim and release on terminal completion. Over-limit work should stay `queued`, not be dropped.

## Acceptance

With a limit of 1, two pushes create two runs, and the second run's jobs are not claimed until the first run's jobs finish.

title: Workflow producer (CIC-84) is never wired into cicado-server: production still creates no jobs
description:
Found in QC of `master` @ `0034d5d` (2026-10-01).

## What's wrong

[CIC-84](https://linear.app/cicadoci/issue/CIC-84/production-workflow-producer-fetch-cicado-workflow-files-at-the-event) is marked Done, but its acceptance ("on a real non-dev-seed server, a signed push webhook ... creates jobs that a runner claims") is not met:

* `controller.NewGitHubWorkflowProducer` has **no non-test caller**. `server/cmd/cicado-server/main.go` sets `ctrlOpts.WorkflowLoader` but never `ctrlOpts.Producer`, so `Config.Producer` is nil and `HandlePush` skips the fetch (`server/controller/controller.go:195`). Outside `-dev-seed`, nothing writes the `workflows` table, which is the same end state [CIC-78](https://linear.app/cicadoci/issue/CIC-78/production-server-creates-runs-but-never-jobs-workflowloader-is-nil) described.
* The producer takes one static `token string` at construction. GitHub App installation tokens expire after 1 hour and are per installation, so even a wired producer would break an hour after start and could only serve one installation. It needs a token source per call: `InstallationTokenMinter` plus an installation-ID lookup (the push payload's `installation.id`, which the payload struct doesn't decode yet).

## Also in the producer (`server/controller/workflowproducer.go`)

* **Deleted workflow files are never removed.** Produce only upserts, so a workflow file deleted from the repo keeps triggering runs forever.
* `ci.yml` and `ci.yaml` both map to name `ci` (`workflowNameFromPath`), which can collide in the store.
* `ContentSHA` is set to the commit SHA, not a hash of the content, so dedup never hits across commits.
* Fetch and upsert failures are logged at Warn and swallowed. The run then proceeds on stale definitions with no signal to the user. A failed check run is the eventual home ([CIC-81](https://linear.app/cicadoci/issue/CIC-81/server-never-reports-check-status-to-github-and-re-run-does-nothing)).

## Fix

1. Wire the producer in `main.go` behind GitHub App config (app ID, private key), with a per-call installation-token source.
2. Decode `installation.id` from push/PR payloads.
3. Inside the upsert, delete workflow rows for the repo whose path is no longer present at the ref.
4. Add a test proving `main`'s controller config has a non-nil Producer when App credentials are configured.

## Acceptance

The [CIC-84](https://linear.app/cicadoci/issue/CIC-84/production-workflow-producer-fetch-cicado-workflow-files-at-the-event) acceptance, run against the shipped binary.

title: Server never reports check status to GitHub, and "Re-run" does nothing: NoOpForge in main.go, rerequest handlers are no-ops

## What's wrong

title: Workflow producer reads .github/workflows/ (GitHub Actions' folder) instead of a CICaDo folder: GitHub Actions also runs those files
description:
Found in QC of `master` @ `0034d5d` (2026-10-01).

## What's wrong

`server/github/workflows.go:96` lists `GET /repos/{o}/{r}/contents/.github/workflows`, and `docs/decisions/CIC-84-workflow-producer.md` documents that choice. But:

* [CIC-84](https://linear.app/cicadoci/issue/CIC-84/production-workflow-producer-fetch-cicado-workflow-files-at-the-event)'s own title says to fetch `.cicado` workflow files.
* `.github/workflows/` belongs to GitHub Actions. GitHub Actions tries to run **every** YAML file there. A CICaDo workflow placed there triggers a failing Actions run ("invalid workflow file") on every push.
* Repos that already use Actions (most of the target users migrating off GHA) have their Actions files fetched and run through the CICaDo parser. Each fails parsing and logs a Warn on every default-branch push. If one happens to parse, CICaDo runs it.

## Fix

* Pick a CICaDo-owned path. The recommendation is `.cicado/workflows/*.y{a}ml` (or `.cicado/*.yml`), matching the ticket title and the `cicado validate` CLI naming.
* Update the fetcher, the decision doc, and `project-docs` together.
* Settle this before the producer is wired in. It is a user-visible convention that is painful to change later.

This needs a product decision on the exact path. Flagged to god.

description:

title: Embedded secret references (e.g. `Bearer ${{ secrets.T }}`) are silently passed through as literal text
description:
Found in QC of `master` @ `f445f0d` (2026-10-02).

## What's wrong

`internal/secretexpr` only recognises a reference when it is the **whole** env value (`secrets.NAME` or `${{ secrets.NAME }}`): see `extract`. For a value such as `Authorization: Bearer ${{ secrets.API_TOKEN }}` or `postgres://u:${{ secrets.PW }}@db`:

* `Refs` doesn't extract it, so the server never delivers the secret.
* `Resolve` leaves it unchanged, so the step receives the literal string `${{ secrets.API_TOKEN }}`.
* `unresolvedSecrets` (`runner/secrets.go:71`) uses the same whole-value `Extract`, so it doesn't flag it. The job doesn't fail clearly; it fails later with a confusing auth error. That is exactly what the unresolved-secret check in `runner/job.go:189` (a PR [cicadoci/core#91](https://linear.app/cicadoci/review/cic-79-deliver-secrets-to-a-job-end-to-end-high-fc8879db8015) review fix) was added to prevent.
* The fork policy (`server/policy/fork.go`, now `secretexpr.IsRef`) also doesn't strip embedded forms. This doesn't leak today, because they are never resolved.

Users coming from GitHub Actions write embedded references all the time.

## Fix (pick one)

1. Support interpolation: scan for every `${{ secrets.NAME }}` occurrence in a value, extract the names, and substitute in place. Then update `unresolvedSecrets` and the fork policy to match.
2. Or reject at parse/validate time: `workflow/parse` returns a positional error for any value containing `secrets.` that isn't a whole-value reference, with a hint.

## Acceptance

A value `Bearer ${{ secrets.T }}` either resolves to `Bearer <value>` or fails `cicado validate` with a line/column error. It never reaches a step as literal text.

title: jobtoken.Postgres.Lookup does not filter kind = 'job' (defence in depth)
description:
Found in QC of `master` @ `0034d5d` (2026-10-01). Low severity.

`server/jobtoken/postgres.go` `Lookup` selects from the shared `tokens` table `WHERE token_hash = $1` without `AND kind = 'job'`. Registration, runner, MCP and API tokens live in the same table with the same sha256 hashing (`server/auth/token.go:72`). Today `Manager.Verify` rejects other kinds by prefix (`auth.Validate(auth.KindJob, raw)`), so this cannot be exploited. But the store's contract shouldn't depend on a caller-side prefix check: runnersvc's own lookups do filter by kind (`service.go:365`).

Separately: `Lookup` scans `expires_at` and `created_by` into non-nullable Go types. A row with NULLs (other kinds have NULLs there) gives a scan error, not a clean not-found.

Fix: add `AND kind = 'job'` to `Lookup` (and to `MarkRevoked` / `SetLastUse`), and add a test that a runner-token hash returns `ErrStoreNotFound`.

title: Workflow `run:` steps can never execute: script becomes argv[0] ("echo hi" exec'd as a program); `uses:` steps have no command
description:
Found in QC of `master` @ `7d8a26a` (2026-10-02).

## What's wrong

`controller.convertSteps` (`server/controller/jobs.go:269`) maps `run: <script>` to `Command: []string{s.Run}`. The runner's shell executor (which `cicanscript` delegates to) runs `exec.CommandContext(step.Command[0], step.Command[1:]...)` (`runner/executor/shell.go:84`). So:

* `run: echo hi` → tries to exec a binary literally named `"echo hi"` → `exec: "echo hi": executable file not found` → the step fails as **infra**.
* Any multi-word or multi-line script fails the same way. Only a bare single-word command like `run: make` would work.
* `uses:` steps get `Command: nil` → `shell: step has no command` → infra failure.

Webhook-created jobs now carry steps ([CIC-104](https://linear.app/cicadoci/issue/CIC-104/webhook-created-jobs-carry-no-steps-and-no-git-checkout-info)), so every real workflow fails at its first step. The e2e tests and dev-seed pass only because they write argv-shaped commands (`["sh","-c",...]` or `["echo","hello"]`) straight into the `steps` table, bypassing `convertSteps`.

## Fix

* Map `run:` to `["/bin/sh", "-ec", script]` (or `bash -eo pipefail -c` when bash is the declared shell), for both shell and docker executors.
* Decide `uses:` semantics for MVP: reject at validate time with a positional error ("`uses:` not supported yet"), or implement it. Don't send command-less steps.
* Add an e2e test that goes YAML → controller → runner (not hand-inserted steps): `run: echo "a b" && echo c` succeeds, and the logs contain both lines.

title: Docker executor: `run:` steps break on images with an ENTRYPOINT (script passed as args to the entrypoint)
description:
Found in QC of `master` @ `ffe228d` (2026-10-03), while reviewing PR [cicadoci/core#112](https://linear.app/cicadoci/review/cic-147-fix-workflow-run-multi-word-execution-uses-rejection-6a70e4503912) ([CIC-147](https://linear.app/cicadoci/issue/CIC-147/workflow-run-steps-can-never-execute-script-becomes-argv0-echo-hi)). That PR's decision doc §2b lists this as a known follow-up, and no ticket existed for it.

## What's wrong

`runner/executor/docker.go` `dockerRunArgs` builds `docker run ... <image> <step.Command...>` (lines \~243–244) and never sets `--entrypoint`. After [CIC-147](https://linear.app/cicadoci/issue/CIC-147/workflow-run-steps-can-never-execute-script-becomes-argv0-echo-hi), a `run:` step's command is `/bin/sh -ec <script>`. For any image with an ENTRYPOINT (for example `golang`-based tool images, `node` images with a custom entrypoint, or most `*/cli` images), Docker runs `<entrypoint> /bin/sh -ec <script>`, so the script is handed to the tool as arguments instead of being executed. GitHub Actions overrides the entrypoint for `run:` steps.

## Fix

For `run:` steps, pass `--entrypoint /bin/sh` and then `-ec <script>`, or have the controller mark steps as shell scripts so the executor can choose. Keep argv-style steps (no shell) unchanged.

## Acceptance

Test with an image whose ENTRYPOINT is not a shell (for example a tiny test image with `ENTRYPOINT ["/bin/false"]`): `run: echo ok` succeeds and prints `ok`.

title: approvalgates.Manager: timeout never enforced, data race in Resolve, callback under lock, gate recorded on failed post, Channel set to PR number
description:
Found in QC of `master` @ `5d6722f` (2026-10-01). Fix these before [CIC-82](https://linear.app/cicadoci/issue/CIC-82/built-but-unwired-subsystems-in-cicado-server-live-log-sse) wires the manager into `cicado-server`.

## What's wrong (`server/approvalgates/approvalgates.go`)

1. **Timeout never enforced.** `Gate.Timeout` is only forwarded to the chat provider. No timer moves a gate to `GateTimedOut`, so a run gated without a click waits forever.
2. **Data race.** `Resolve` unlocks, then reads `rec.State` for `onResolved(runID, rec.State)`, which can race with `CloseAll`. Use the copied state.
3. **Callback and network I/O under lock.** `CloseAll` calls `provider.CloseApproval` and `onResolved` while holding `m.mu`. A callback that calls `State()` deadlocks. `Open` also holds `m.mu` across `RequestApproval` (a Slack HTTP call), which serialises every gate.
4. **Ghost gate on failure.** `Open` stores the record before `RequestApproval`. If the post fails, a pending gate with no message stays in the map.
5. `State()` **of an unknown run returns** `GatePending`**.** Callers cannot tell "no gate" from "waiting". Return `(state, ok)`.
6. **Controller misuse.** `controller.maybeOpenGate` (`server/controller/controller.go:369`) sets `Channel` to the PR number (`"42"`), not a chat channel ID. It also opens a gate for every PR run, with an empty allow-list by default, so the buttons cannot be used.
7. Gates live only in memory and are lost on restart.

## Fix

Points 1–5 in the manager, with `-race` tests. Point 6: channel from config, and open gates only when policy requires it. Point 7: track as a follow-up (persist gates in Postgres).

title: HTTP API is unauthenticated in the shipped binary: live job logs (GET /api/v1/logs?job=) readable by anyone; no per-org authorization
description:
Found in QC of `master` @ `7d8a26a` (2026-10-02).

## What's wrong

* `server/cmd/cicado-server/main.go:270` builds `api.New(st, WithLogger, WithWebhookReceiver, WithSSEHandler)` with no authenticator, so the default no-op authenticator is used (`handler.go:208`: "noOpAuthenticator keeps it open today").
* [CIC-82](https://linear.app/cicadoci/issue/CIC-82/built-but-unwired-subsystems-in-cicado-server-live-log-sse) ([cicadoci/core#94](https://linear.app/cicadoci/review/cic-82-wire-live-log-streaming-sse-route-masked-logpublish-a55d9822c081)) added `GET /api/v1/logs?job=<id>`, which streams a job's full log history and live tail. Its decision doc and tests cite "auth on both chains", but in the shipped binary that auth is the no-op. **Anyone who can reach the HTTP port can read any job's logs**, plus the existing run and runner read endpoints. Logs are masked for registered secrets but routinely contain other sensitive output (internal hostnames, tokens from tools, PII in test fixtures).
* Even with a real authenticator, `logs.SSE.ServeHTTP` only parses `?job=`. There's no check that the caller's org owns the job's repo, so it is cross-tenant readable by job UUID.

[CIC-44](https://linear.app/cicadoci/issue/CIC-44/auth-github-oauth-login-adminmember-roles) (GitHub OAuth login) is the planned real auth, but it's in Backlog, and nothing stops a production deploy from exposing these routes today.

## Fix

1. Until [CIC-44](https://linear.app/cicadoci/issue/CIC-44/auth-github-oauth-login-adminmember-roles) lands: require a configured API token (static bearer, or an `api`-kind token from the `tokens` table) and refuse to serve `/api/v1/*` (except webhooks and health) without one. Fail closed, like [CIC-80](https://linear.app/cicadoci/issue/CIC-80/webhook-signature-verification-is-silently-disabled-when-cicado) did for webhooks. Add a dev opt-in flag.
2. In the SSE handler (and the run/job read handlers), authorize: resolve job → run → repo → org, and compare with the principal's org.
3. Fix the [CIC-82](https://linear.app/cicadoci/issue/CIC-82/built-but-unwired-subsystems-in-cicado-server-live-log-sse) decision doc wording ("authenticated" means a no-op today).

## Acceptance

A request without credentials to `/api/v1/logs?job=` gets 401. A principal from org A requesting org B's job gets 404 or 403.

title: Secrets leak via flag defaults: --webhook-secret, --secret-key, GitHub token flags print env values in usage output
description:
Found by Dwight in review of PR [cicadoci/core#116](https://linear.app/cicadoci/review/featapi-fail-closed-bearer-token-auth-on-apiv1-cic-150-c0eedbfdc470) ([CIC-150](https://linear.app/cicadoci/issue/CIC-150/http-api-is-unauthenticated-in-the-shipped-binary-live-job-logs-get)).

In `server/cmd/cicado-server/main.go`, secret-bearing flags take their default from `os.Getenv(...)`. Go's `flag` package prints defaults in usage text, so `--help` or any mistyped flag prints the secret to stderr and logs. Reproduced: `CICADO_API_TOKEN=LEAKME-api cicado-server --bogus` prints `(default "LEAKME-api")`. Same leak confirmed for `--webhook-secret`, `--secret-key` (the AES key) and the GitHub token flags.

## Fix

Give each flag an empty default and read the env var after `flag.Parse()` (or use a `flag.Value` whose `String()` returns ""). Add a test asserting no secret appears in `PrintDefaults` output.

## Acceptance

With all secret env vars set, an invalid flag prints no secret value.

title: Runner never checks out the repository: GitContext (clone URL/ref/SHA) is sent but ignored, jobs run in an empty workspace
description:
Found in QC of `master` @ `7d8a26a` (2026-10-02).

## What's wrong

[CIC-104](https://linear.app/cicadoci/issue/CIC-104/webhook-created-jobs-carry-no-steps-and-no-git-checkout-info) ([cicadoci/core#100](https://linear.app/cicadoci/review/cic-104-persist-gitcloneurlgitrefgitsha-in-convertjobspecs-9925a9eb1022)) persists `git_clone_url`, `git_ref` and `git_sha`, and the server sends them in `JobAssignment.Git` (`server/runnersvc/session.go`). But **nothing in** `runner/` **reads them**: there are no references to `GetGit`, `CloneUrl` or `git clone` anywhere in the runner. Every job's workspace is an empty temp dir, so `make test`, `go test ./...` and similar can't work on any repo.

Private repos also need credentials. The stored URL is token-less (`https://github.com/<o>/<r>.git`, which is correct per the "no secrets in assignments" invariant). The per-job installation token from [CIC-26](https://linear.app/cicadoci/issue/CIC-26/per-job-github-installation-tokens-for-clone-never-persisted) (`forge.CloneCredentialsForRun`) is not delivered anywhere.

## Fix

1. Runner: in `Prepare` (all executors), when `Git.CloneUrl` is set, do a shallow fetch of `Git.Sha` (or `Ref`) into the workspace: `git init`, `git fetch --depth=1 origin <sha>`, `git checkout FETCH_HEAD`. A failure there is an infra failure with a clear detail message.
2. Credentials: deliver a short-lived clone token **only** through a lease-scoped RPC (extend `GetJobSecrets` with a reserved clone-credential entry, or add a sibling RPC). Never put it in the assignment or journal. Register it with the masker. Don't use a token for fork runs of public repos.
3. Add an e2e test: a job against a local bare git repo (`file://`) checks out the expected SHA, and a step can `cat` a file from it.

title: `make dev` broken: server exits at startup since CIC-150 — docker-compose sets neither CICADO_API_TOKEN nor CICADO_INSECURE_API
description:
Found in QC of `master` @ `89cd97f` (2026-10-04).

[cicadoci/core#116](https://linear.app/cicadoci/review/featapi-fail-closed-bearer-token-auth-on-apiv1-cic-150-c0eedbfdc470) ([CIC-150](https://linear.app/cicadoci/issue/CIC-150/http-api-is-unauthenticated-in-the-shipped-binary-live-job-logs-get)) added `apiStartupGuard` (`server/cmd/cicado-server/main.go:150`, `:498`). The server now refuses to start when `CICADO_API_TOKEN` is empty and `--insecure-api` / `CICADO_INSECURE_API` is not set. Unlike the ephemeral-key guard, `--dev-seed` does **not** bypass it.

`docker-compose.yml` (the `server` service, lines 44–55) sets `CICADO_INSECURE_WEBHOOK` for the [CIC-80](https://linear.app/cicadoci/issue/CIC-80/webhook-signature-verification-is-silently-disabled-when-cicado) guard but has nothing for the API guard. So `make dev` ([README.md:37](<http://README.md:37>), docs/development.md:13) brings up a server that exits immediately with "CICADO_API_TOKEN is not set and --insecure-api was not passed". The runner never becomes healthy, and the documented dev loop is broken. This is the same class of regression [CIC-80](https://linear.app/cicadoci/issue/CIC-80/webhook-signature-verification-is-silently-disabled-when-cicado) caused and fixed in compose.

CI doesn't catch it: the Docker images job builds the images but never runs compose.

## Fix

1. Add `CICADO_INSECURE_API: "true"` to the compose `server` env, with a comment like the one for the webhook flag. Or set a fixed dev `CICADO_API_TOKEN` and document it for `curl`/SSE use in docs/development.md.
2. Add a CI smoke step (`docker compose up -d --wait` plus a health probe), or a test that parses `docker-compose.yml` env and runs the startup guards against it, so a new fail-closed guard can't silently break `make dev` again.
3. Small cleanup while in `main.go`: the secrets-store comment block at lines \~180–189 is still duplicated (listed in [CIC-83](https://linear.app/cicadoci/issue/CIC-83/cleanup-stalemisattributed-todos-and-code-comments-abandoned), which is Done).

## Acceptance

`make dev` on a clean checkout gets the server healthy and the demo job runs. The CI check fails if compose can't boot the server.

title: Private repos can never be cloned: per-job clone token (CIC-26) is built but never minted or delivered (TokenMinter nil in main.go, Auth stub)
description:
Found in QC of `master` @ `ffe228d` (2026-10-03).

## What's wrong

[CIC-26](https://linear.app/cicadoci/issue/CIC-26/per-job-github-installation-tokens-for-clone-never-persisted) ("Per-job GitHub installation tokens for clone") is Done, but nothing in the shipped binary uses it:

* `server/cmd/cicado-server/main.go:399` `newForge` builds `forge.NewGitHubForge(..., nil)`, so the TokenMinter is **nil**, and `CloneCredentialsForRun` always returns `errNoMinter`.
* `forge.CloneCredentialsForRun` has **no non-test caller** in `server/` or `runner/`.
* `github.InstallationTokenMinter.Auth` is documented as "a stub that returns a static token; full JWT implementation is [CIC-26](https://linear.app/cicadoci/issue/CIC-26/per-job-github-installation-tokens-for-clone-never-persisted)+". No App-JWT signing exists.
* The clone URL is `https://github.com/<repo>.git` with no credentials (`controller.go:208`), and the synthetic checkout step from PR [cicadoci/core#112](https://linear.app/cicadoci/review/cic-147-fix-workflow-run-multi-word-execution-uses-rejection-6a70e4503912) ([CIC-147](https://linear.app/cicadoci/issue/CIC-147/workflow-run-steps-can-never-execute-script-becomes-argv0-echo-hi)/148) clones it anonymously.

Result: once [CIC-147](https://linear.app/cicadoci/issue/CIC-147/workflow-run-steps-can-never-execute-script-becomes-argv0-echo-hi)/148 land, **every job on a private repository fails at checkout**. Most self-hosted CI users have private repos.

## Constraints

* The token must never go in the step `Command` or the `JobAssignment`. Steps are persisted, and secrets may only travel through the lease-scoped `GetJobSecrets` (security invariant).
* Register the token with the masker (`RegisterWithVariants`, [CIC-74](https://linear.app/cicadoci/issue/CIC-74/redaction-masker-never-learns-a-real-secret-value-in-production)) before use.

## Fix

1. Implement App-JWT `Auth` (RS256 with the App private key) and wire `InstallationTokenMinterAdapter` into `newForge` from App ID + key flags. Share this with [CIC-146](https://linear.app/cicadoci/issue/CIC-146/workflow-producer-mint-installation-tokens-per-call-and-decode), which needs the same minter.
2. Mint per job at lease time. Deliver it through `GetJobSecrets` under a reserved name (for example `CICADO_GIT_TOKEN`), and have the checkout step use a git credential helper (`git -c credential.helper=...`) or `http.extraHeader` read from env, never the URL.
3. Fork PRs: still read-only, with a contents:read installation token scoped to the base repo only.

## Acceptance

E2E: a job for a repo whose fetch requires auth checks out successfully. The token never appears in `jobs.steps`, the assignment, or logs (masked).
