title: Workflow producer: mint installation tokens per call and decode installation.id from webhooks (CIC-120 follow-up)
description:
Follow-up split out of [CIC-120](https://linear.app/cicadoci/issue/CIC-120/workflow-producer-cic-84-is-never-wired-into-cicado-server-production) (PR [cicadoci/core#106](https://linear.app/cicadoci/review/cic-120-wire-the-github-workflow-producer-into-cicado-server-efdea3f25c9f)), per god's option (b) decision on Dwight's review.

## Context

PR [cicadoci/core#106](https://linear.app/cicadoci/review/cic-120-wire-the-github-workflow-producer-into-cicado-server-efdea3f25c9f) wires `controller.GitHubWorkflowProducer` into `cicado-server` behind `--github-workflow-token` / `CICADO_GITHUB_WORKFLOW_TOKEN`. That flag takes one static token, documented as a long-lived **fine-grained personal access token** (contents:read). This is an MVP: it serves only the repos that PAT can read, and the operator owns its rotation.

A GitHub App installation token cannot be used there: it expires after 1 hour and is scoped to one installation, so fetches would start failing with 401 an hour after start (logged at Warn and swallowed, so runs would silently use stale definitions).

## Scope

1. Replace the producer's static `token string` with a per-call token source (for example `func(ctx, installationID int64) (string, error)`), backed by the existing `github.InstallationTokenMinter` / `InstallationTokenMinterAdapter` ([CIC-26](https://linear.app/cicadoci/issue/CIC-26/per-job-github-installation-tokens-for-clone-never-persisted), [CIC-81](https://linear.app/cicadoci/issue/CIC-81/server-never-reports-check-status-to-github-and-re-run-does-nothing)).
2. Configure it from GitHub App credentials (app ID + private key) in `main.go`; keep the PAT flag as an optional fallback or remove it.
3. Decode `installation.id` from push and pull_request webhook payloads and pass it through `HandlePush` to `Produce`.
4. Test: two installations served by one server; a token minted after expiry is refreshed; main wiring builds the producer from App credentials.

## Acceptance

A default-branch push in any repo of any installation of the App upserts that repo's workflows, including more than 1 hour after server start. The `TODO` at the producer construction site in `server/cmd/cicado-server/main.go` is removed.

title: Docker executor timeout doesn't kill the step on Linux: TestDockerTimeoutKillsStep fails on every CI run (masked by CIC-190); container also left running
description:
Found in QC of `master` @ `29cf433` (2026-10-05). [CIC-190](https://linear.app/cicadoci/issue/CIC-190/ci-never-fails-on-test-failures-go-test-tee-jq-sed-runs-without) (no pipefail) has hidden this failure.

## Evidence

* CI Test (race), run 37249140979 (`29cf433`): `docker_test.go:297: timeout took 30.003262318s; the step was not killed promptly`, `--- FAIL: TestDockerTimeoutKillsStep (30.00s)`, `FAIL cicadoci.com/cicado/runner/executor`.
* The same failure shows on every non-cancelled master run checked, back to 2026-09-24 (`cfb42c2`). The job was green each time.
* It passes locally on macOS. The full local suite on `29cf433` passes: 39/39 packages.

## Root cause

`runner/executor/docker.go` RunStep (\~:135–160) runs `exec.CommandContext(stepCtx, docker, ...)`. On timeout it SIGKILLs **only the** `docker` **client process**. There's no process group (`Setpgid`) and no `cmd.WaitDelay`, and it then blocks in `wg.Wait()` on the stdout/stderr pumps until **every** holder of the pipe's write end exits.

In the test, the fake docker script (`docker_test.go`, ends with `exec "$@"`) runs `sh -c "sleep 30"`. On Ubuntu `/bin/sh` is dash, which **forks** `sleep` instead of exec'ing it, so the grandchild `sleep` keeps the pipes open for 30 s after the client is killed. On macOS `/bin/sh` is bash, which exec's the last command, so the test passes there.

The production version is worse. Killing the `docker run` client (SIGKILL, so no sig-proxy) does **not** stop the container. That's the known limitation at `docker.go:46–48`/`:114` ("deferred to [CIC-16](https://linear.app/cicadoci/issue/CIC-16/step-engine-env-injection-exit-codes-timeouts-cancellation-propagation)"), but [CIC-16](https://linear.app/cicadoci/issue/CIC-16/step-engine-env-injection-exit-codes-timeouts-cancellation-propagation) is Done and no ticket tracks it. A timed-out or cancelled step's container keeps running on the runner host, consuming resources and possibly writing to the mounted workspace while the next step or job runs.

## Fix

1. Give each step a known container name (`--name cicado-<job>-<step>-<rand>`) or `--cidfile`. On timeout or cancel, run `docker kill <name>` (then `docker rm -f`), then reap the client.
2. Set `cmd.WaitDelay` (for example 5 s) so pumps can never hang past the deadline, and/or `Setpgid` plus group kill as in `shell.go`.
3. Make the test platform-independent: use `Command: []string{"sleep", "30"}` (exec'd directly) or have the fake script exec in its own process group, and assert that the container-kill call happens.
4. Land this before, or together with, [CIC-190](https://linear.app/cicadoci/issue/CIC-190/ci-never-fails-on-test-failures-go-test-tee-jq-sed-runs-without), so master doesn't go red when pipefail is fixed.

## Acceptance

TestDockerTimeoutKillsStep passes on Linux CI with pipefail on. A real-docker test (behind a build tag) shows a timed-out step's container is gone within a few seconds.

title: CI never fails on test failures: `go test | tee | jq | sed` runs without pipefail, so a failing Test (race) step stays green
description:
Found by Dwight on PR [cicadoci/core#134](https://linear.app/cicadoci/review/featcontrollermain-wire-per-call-github-app-installation-token-minter-6191f7213e4d) (issuecomment-5986810361) and verified on `master` @ `29cf433` (2026-10-05).

## What's wrong

`.github/workflows/ci.yml:114` (the "Run tests with the race detector" step):

```
run: go test ./... -race -count=1 -timeout 15m -json | tee /tmp/test-output.json | jq -r 'select(.Action == "output") | .Output' | sed '/^$/d'
```

The workflow sets no `shell:` and has no `defaults.run.shell`. When `shell` is unspecified, GitHub runs steps with `bash -e {0}`, which has **no** `pipefail`. The step's exit status is `sed`'s, which is always 0. **A failing test never fails the job.** The following "Fail if any test was skipped" step only checks skips, not failures.

## Evidence

* PR [cicadoci/core#134](https://linear.app/cicadoci/review/featcontrollermain-wire-per-call-github-app-installation-token-minter-6191f7213e4d) run 37251166516: `TestCIC180_B1_MinterBeatsPAT` failed, and the job was green.
* Master: `TestDockerTimeoutKillsStep` has failed on **every** non-cancelled master run checked, as far back as 2026-09-24 (`cfb42c2` … `29cf433`, run 37249140979), and every run is green. It's tracked separately as its own bug.
* The pipeline has been in place since about 2026-09-17, so the "Test (race)" check hasn't gated anything since then.

## Fix

1. Add `shell: bash` to that step (GitHub then uses `bash --noprofile --norc -eo pipefail {0}`), or set `defaults: run: shell: bash` for the whole workflow, or start the `run:` with `set -o pipefail`.
2. Belt and braces: add a step that fails when `/tmp/test-output.json` contains any `"Action":"fail"` event, for example `jq -e 'select(.Action=="fail")' /tmp/test-output.json && exit 1 || true`, written so a `jq` error can't pass silently. This also catches a failing package whose summary line gets lost.
3. Audit the other multi-command `run:` steps in `ci.yml` for the same pattern.

## Acceptance

A deliberately failing test on a throwaway branch turns the Test (race) job red. Before merging this, the known master failure (`TestDockerTimeoutKillsStep`, separate ticket) must be fixed or marked skip-with-ticket, or master goes red.

title: Security: docker executor passes step env (incl. resolved secrets) as `docker run -e KEY=VALUE` argv — world-readable via ps on the runner host
description:
Found in the post-pipefail sweep on `master` @ `582b06c` (2026-10-05), from reading `runner/executor/docker.go`.

## What's wrong

`dockerRunArgs` (`runner/executor/docker.go` \~:225–240) adds every step env var as `-e KEY=VALUE` on the `docker` client's command line. `runner/job.go` builds the step env with `secretexpr.Resolve(stepRaw, secrets)`, so secrets from `GetJobSecrets` are **already resolved to their plaintext values** by then, including `github_clone_token` ([CIC-148](https://linear.app/cicadoci/issue/CIC-148/runner-never-checks-out-the-repository-gitcontext-clone-urlrefsha-is)/151). The file's own doc comment (`docker.go:53–60`) admits that argv is "world-readable via `ps` / /proc/<pid>/cmdline by *any* local user, no privilege needed", but nothing tracks it as a defect.

On a shared or self-hosted runner host, any local process or user (another job using the shell executor, a monitoring agent, a compromised service account) can read job secrets while the container starts. That breaks the secrets invariant: values travel only through the lease-scoped `GetJobSecrets`, are held in memory only, and are never exposed beyond the job. The masker doesn't help here because it only scrubs log output.

## Fix

Pass values without putting them in argv:

* `-e KEY` (name only) with the value set in the `docker` client's own `cmd.Env`. Docker then copies it from the client's environment, which is readable only by the owning UID and root, the same exposure as the shell executor. Or:
* `--env-file` pointing at a 0600 temp file in a 0700 dir, deleted right after the container starts.

Add a test asserting no secret value ever appears in `dockerRunArgs` output, using a fake docker that dumps its argv.

The docker executor isn't selectable in production yet ([CIC-132](https://linear.app/cicadoci/issue/CIC-132/per-job-executor-selection-stop-hardcoding-cicanscript-in)), so this isn't exploitable today. It must be fixed before [CIC-132](https://linear.app/cicadoci/issue/CIC-132/per-job-executor-selection-stop-hardcoding-cicanscript-in) ships, which is why it's High.

## Acceptance

With a step env holding a resolved secret, the docker client's argv (`/proc/<pid>/cmdline`) contains only `-e KEY`, never the value. The container still sees the right value.

title: Docker executor never stops the container on timeout/cancel (CIC-191 fixed only the client); real-docker tests never run in CI
description:
Found in the post-pipefail hidden-failure sweep on `master` @ `582b06c` (2026-10-05).

## Container still leaks

[CIC-191](https://linear.app/cicadoci/issue/CIC-191/docker-executor-timeout-doesnt-kill-the-step-on-linux)'s PR ([cicadoci/core#136](https://linear.app/cicadoci/review/fixes-cic-191-docker-executor-timeout-kills-client-fb722e95dadd), `d6b68c2`, 1 file) put the `docker` client in its own process group and SIGKILLs the group on timeout or cancel (`runner/executor/docker.go:138–144`). That fixed the hanging test. But the second half of [CIC-191](https://linear.app/cicadoci/issue/CIC-191/docker-executor-timeout-doesnt-kill-the-step-on-linux) (kill the **container**) wasn't done: there's no `--name`/`--cidfile` and no `docker kill`/`rm -f` anywhere in `docker.go`. The doc comment still says so (`docker.go:46–51`: "we do not yet track the container ID ... A killed client can leave its `--rm` container running ... [CIC-16](https://linear.app/cicadoci/issue/CIC-16/step-engine-env-injection-exit-codes-timeouts-cancellation-propagation) adds that path"). [CIC-16](https://linear.app/cicadoci/issue/CIC-16/step-engine-env-injection-exit-codes-timeouts-cancellation-propagation) is Done, and [CIC-191](https://linear.app/cicadoci/issue/CIC-191/docker-executor-timeout-doesnt-kill-the-step-on-linux) auto-closed on merge ("Fixes [CIC-191](https://linear.app/cicadoci/issue/CIC-191/docker-executor-timeout-doesnt-kill-the-step-on-linux)"). A SIGKILLed client doesn't proxy the signal, so a timed-out or cancelled step's container keeps running on the runner host, still writing to the bind-mounted workspace, while the next step or job runs.

## Real-docker tests never run

`runner/executor/docker_real_test.go` (`//go:build docker`, `TestDockerRealEgressOff`) is the only test against a real daemon. Its header says "CI's test job has no docker", but GitHub's `ubuntu-latest` runners ship Docker (the CI **Docker images** job uses it in the same workflow, run 37304446928). No CI job passes `-tags docker`, so real-runtime behaviour has never run in CI: `--network none`, the [CIC-152](https://linear.app/cicadoci/issue/CIC-152/docker-executor-run-steps-break-on-images-with-an-entrypoint-script) `--entrypoint ""` override, and timeout/cancel teardown.

## Fix

1. Name each step's container (`--name cicado-<job>-<step>-<rand>`) or use `--cidfile`. In `cmd.Cancel` (and on any error path), run `docker kill <name>` then `docker rm -f <name>` with a short bounded context, then kill the client group. Update the stale `docker.go:46–51` / `:166–168` comments.
2. Add a CI step (or job) running `go test -tags docker -race ./runner/executor/...` on `ubuntu-latest`. Add real tests for: a timeout removes the container (`docker ps -a --filter name=...` is empty within about 5 s); an image with a non-shell ENTRYPOINT runs `run:`; `--network none` blocks egress.

The docker executor isn't selectable in production yet (executor is hard-coded to `cicanscript`, [CIC-132](https://linear.app/cicadoci/issue/CIC-132/per-job-executor-selection-stop-hardcoding-cicanscript-in)), so this is Medium. It has to be fixed before [CIC-132](https://linear.app/cicadoci/issue/CIC-132/per-job-executor-selection-stop-hardcoding-cicanscript-in) ships.

## Acceptance

The `-tags docker` CI step is green and includes a test proving the container is gone after a step timeout.

title: Remove the superseded forge.TokenMinter clone path (puts the token in the clone URL); fix stale fork-token comment in secretRefsFor
description:
Found in QC of `master` @ `d0293a2` (2026-10-04).

[CIC-148](https://linear.app/cicadoci/issue/CIC-148/runner-never-checks-out-the-repository-gitcontext-clone-urlrefsha-is) ([cicadoci/core#123](https://linear.app/cicadoci/review/featcontroller-per-repo-github-clone-token-delivery-cic-148-dd23221c3b04)) and [CIC-151](https://linear.app/cicadoci/issue/CIC-151/private-repos-can-never-be-cloned-per-job-clone-token-cic-26-is-built) ([cicadoci/core#124](https://linear.app/cicadoci/review/featclonerunnersvc-cic-151-per-job-github-app-installation-token-a0600362c927)) shipped the real clone-credential path. `runnersvc.CloneMinterFunc` (`server/runnersvc/clone_minter.go`) mints a contents:read, single-repo token at lease time. It's delivered only via `GetJobSecrets` and used through a `git -c credential.helper` in the checkout step (`server/controller/jobs.go:255`, `:383`), so it's never persisted or put in a URL.

The older, never-wired path is still in the tree and is now abandoned code:

* `forge.Forge.CloneCredentialsForRun` / `forge.TokenMinter` (`server/forge/forge.go:38`, `server/forge/github.go:26–83`). `newForge` still passes a nil minter (`server/cmd/cicado-server/main.go:583`).
* `github.InstallationTokenMinterAdapter` (`server/github/forge_adapter.go:58–131`), `CloneCredentialsForRunOnClient` (`server/github/installation.go:210`), and `cloneURLWithToken` (`:240`). The last one **embeds the token in the clone URL** (`https://x-access-token:TOKEN@github.com/...`). That's exactly the pattern the new design avoids, because URLs end up in `git remote -v`, `.git/config`, process lists and error output. If anyone wires this path later "because it exists", the token leaks.
* Stubs: `ChecksClient.CloneCredentialsForRun` and `errNoCloneCreds` (`server/github/checks.go:262–282`), and `NoOpForge.CloneCredentialsForRun` (`server/controller/noop.go:48`).

Also a stale comment: `server/controller/jobs.go:282–286` says "non-fork runs get the static installation token". Since [cicadoci/core#124](https://linear.app/cicadoci/review/featclonerunnersvc-cic-151-per-job-github-app-installation-token-a0600362c927), fork and non-fork both get a freshly minted contents:read token (`ClonePermissions = "read"`, `clone_minter.go`), and the `isFork` argument to the minter closure is unused.

## Fix

Delete `CloneCredentialsForRun` from the `forge.Forge` interface and from all implementations, along with the adapter, `CloneCredentialsForRunOnClient` and `cloneURLWithToken`, and their tests. Update the comment. If a per-fork permission difference is ever wanted, use `isFork` explicitly.

## Acceptance

`grep -rn "CloneCredentialsForRun\|cloneURLWithToken" server` returns nothing. Build, vet, lint and tests stay green.

## Also: no env fallback for the App credentials

`--github-app-id` and `--github-app-key-file` (`server/cmd/cicado-server/main.go:117–118`) are flag-only. Every other server setting has a `CICADO_*` env equivalent (`envBool`/`envSecret`), and docker-compose and container deploys configure through env. Add `CICADO_GITHUB_APP_ID` and `CICADO_GITHUB_APP_KEY_FILE`, read the same way, and add a test.

title: Approval gates cannot gate anything: Manager never built in main.go, nothing calls Resolve, gate state never blocks dispatch, decisions not audited
description:
Found in QC of `master` @ `21c5306` (2026-10-03), after [CIC-108](https://linear.app/cicadoci/issue/CIC-108/approvalgatesmanager-timeout-never-enforced-data-race-in-resolve) ([cicadoci/core#118](https://linear.app/cicadoci/review/fixapprovalgates-fix-4-manager-sub-bugs-auto-timeout-race-callback-8f098d6049b5)) fixed the Manager's internal bugs.

`server/approvalgates` is now internally correct, but the feature is a dead end on every side:

1. **Never constructed.** Nothing in `server/cmd/cicado-server` sets `controller.Config.ApprovalGates` or `AllowedApprovers`, so `maybeOpenGate` (`controller.go:694`) returns early.
2. **Nothing can resolve a gate.** `Manager.Resolve` and `CloseAll` have no non-test callers. There is no Slack interaction handler on master ([CIC-138](https://linear.app/cicadoci/issue/CIC-138/no-real-slack-integration-on-master-cic-49-socket-mode-events-api-is)), and no API or MCP route.
3. **A gate doesn't gate.** Nothing outside the package reads `Manager.State`, and `onResolved` isn't wired to the queue or dispatch. Even if a gate opened, the run's jobs would dispatch regardless. `maybeOpenGate` opens one "for every PR run as a placeholder".
4. **No audit trail.** Approve, deny, unauthorized-click and timeout transitions write no audit event. That breaks the invariant "every state change writes an audit event" and the M7 exit criterion "unauthorized approval attempts are rejected and audited" (plan line 104).
5. Channel and timeout source: tracked separately in [CIC-160](https://linear.app/cicadoci/issue/CIC-160/approvalgates-controllermaybeopengate-sets-channel-to-the-pr-number).

## Fix

* Gate on a workflow-declared approval (`environment:` or a gate step), not on every PR run. Hold dependent jobs in `pending` until the gate is approved. Fail or skip them on deny or timeout.
* Call `Resolve` from the Slack interaction handler ([CIC-138](https://linear.app/cicadoci/issue/CIC-138/no-real-slack-integration-on-master-cic-49-socket-mode-events-api-is)), passing the acting user. Add an audited API endpoint for the non-Slack path.
* Emit audit events for every transition, including rejected unauthorized clicks.
* Construct the Manager in `main.go` when a chat provider is configured.

## Acceptance

An e2e test where a workflow with a gate opens a gate and the gated job doesn't dispatch. An authorized approve dispatches it. An unauthorized click is rejected, and both write audit rows. Timeout fails the job.

title: Audit: PostgresLog.Append hard-codes principal_type='user' (and surface='system', org_id NULL) for every event, including system actors
description:
From Dwight's [cicadoci/core#135](https://linear.app/cicadoci/review/refs-cic-162-part-1-build-the-approvalgates-manager-in-cicado-server-8f3ee4d60eb3) READY review (issuecomment-5989744248). Verified in code on `master` @ `29cf433` and on PR [cicadoci/core#135](https://linear.app/cicadoci/review/refs-cic-162-part-1-build-the-approvalgates-manager-in-cicado-server-8f3ee4d60eb3).

## What's wrong

`server/audit/postgres.go:85–95` inserts every audit row with literal values:

```sql
INSERT INTO audit_events (org_id, principal_type, principal_id, surface, ...)
VALUES (NULL, 'user', $1, 'system', ...)
```

`audit.Entry` (`server/audit/audit.go:43`) has only a free-text `Actor`, with no principal type, org or surface. So every row is recorded as a **user**, whatever really acted:

* Approval-gate timeout: [cicadoci/core#135](https://linear.app/cicadoci/review/refs-cic-162-part-1-build-the-approvalgates-manager-in-cicado-server-8f3ee4d60eb3) `gateAuditEntry` (`server/cmd/cicado-server/main.go:750–768`) sets `Actor = "system"`, and the row says `principal_type='user', principal_id='system'`.
* Check-run rerequest: `controller.go:437` `Actor: "github-rerequest"`.
* Job-token audit: `server/jobtoken/audit.go:41–71`, where the issuer is a server component.

The schema already supports the right values: `principal_type CHECK IN ('user','runner','agent','token','system')` (`server/store/migrations/0001_init.sql:416–418`), plus an `org_id` FK and a `surface` column. Filtering the audit log by principal type (`audit_events_principal_idx`, `0001_init.sql:432`) can't distinguish human actions from automatic ones, which undermines the "every state change is audited" invariant for review purposes. Every row also has `org_id NULL` and `surface='system'`, so per-org audit queries return nothing.

## Fix (one line)

Add `PrincipalType`, `OrgID` and `Surface` to `audit.Entry` and bind them in the INSERT instead of the literals (default `PrincipalType` to `"system"` when the actor is a server component, and set `"user"` only for a real human actor).

Notes:

* Keep `hashEntry` (`audit.go:114`) stable, or version it. Adding fields to the hashed struct changes every new hash, so decide deliberately and test chain verification across the change.
* Update the callers above to set the correct type (gate timeout → `system`; approve/deny → `user`; job tokens → `token`/`system`).

## Acceptance

A gate timeout writes `principal_type='system'`. An approve writes `'user'` with the acting user's ID. Run-creation rows carry the run's `org_id`. A test reads them back and asserts each.

title: approvalgates onResolved audit write uses run()'s signal ctx, so gate resolutions during shutdown are never audited
description:
From Dwight's [cicadoci/core#135](https://linear.app/cicadoci/review/refs-cic-162-part-1-build-the-approvalgates-manager-in-cicado-server-8f3ee4d60eb3) READY review (issuecomment-5989744248). Verified in PR [cicadoci/core#135](https://linear.app/cicadoci/review/refs-cic-162-part-1-build-the-approvalgates-manager-in-cicado-server-8f3ee4d60eb3) (`knowroozi/cic-162-approvalgates-wiring`).

## What's wrong

`server/cmd/cicado-server/main.go` ([cicadoci/core#135](https://linear.app/cicadoci/review/refs-cic-162-part-1-build-the-approvalgates-manager-in-cicado-server-8f3ee4d60eb3)):

* `:195`: `ctx, stop := signal.NotifyContext(context.Background(), os.Interrupt, syscall.SIGTERM)`
* `:399`: `buildApprovalGates(ctx, ...)` receives that ctx
* `:727–734`: the `onResolved` closure captures it and calls `auditLog.Append(ctx, e)`

On SIGTERM/SIGINT the ctx is cancelled first, while the gate Manager's `time.AfterFunc` timeout timers keep running. A gate that times out (`onTimeout` → `GateTimedOut` → `onResolved`) or is resolved while the server drains then fails its audit append with `context canceled` (logged as "approvalgates: audit append failed"), so **those gate state changes are never audited**. (Correction: no shutdown code calls `Manager.CloseAll` today. Pending gates are simply abandoned on shutdown, with no terminal audit row. Decide whether shutdown should `CloseAll` them, which would then hit this same bug.) That breaks the "every state change writes an audit event" invariant. A long-running server's ctx also ties a per-event write to the process lifetime instead of giving it its own deadline.

## Fix (one line)

In `onResolved`, write with a fresh, bounded context detached from cancellation: `actx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.WithoutCancel(ctx), 5*time.Second); defer cancel(); auditLog.Append(actx, e)`. Also make sure shutdown waits for in-flight audit writes before closing the DB pool.

## Acceptance

A test cancels the ctx passed to `buildApprovalGates`, then calls `CloseAll` on an open gate, and asserts that the timeout audit row is written.

title: No operator surface to set secrets or cancel/rerun a run: secrets.Put and queue.RequestCancel have no production caller; 7 of 8 audit actions are never written
description:
Found in QC of `master` @ `29cf433` (2026-10-05).

The MVP definition (`project-docs/01-project-plan.md:13`) needs jobs "with ... secrets", plus cancel and rerun. Server-side engines exist for both, but nothing in the shipped binaries can reach them.

## Secrets can't be written

* `secrets.Postgres.Put` (`server/secrets/postgres.go:66`) has **no non-test caller**.
* There's no API route: `server/api/handler.go:162–175` serves only healthz, readyz, `GET runs`, `GET runs/{id}`, `GET runners`, `POST validate` and webhooks.
* There's no CLI: `cmd/cicado/main.go:54` has only `validate`. The MCP server is read-only by design.
* Values are AES-encrypted with `CICADO_SECRET_KEY`, so an operator can't insert them with SQL either.
* [CIC-37](https://linear.app/cicadoci/issue/CIC-37/secrets-store-kms-envelope-encryption-scoping-write-only-api) ("write-only API") is Done, but the write-only *API* was never exposed. Result: `GetJobSecrets` delivery ([CIC-38](https://linear.app/cicadoci/issue/CIC-38/getjobsecrets-rpc-lease-authorized-delivery-memory-only-on-runner)/79) works only in tests, which call `secretStore.Put` directly (`test/e2e/skeleton_test.go` TestSecretDelivery). In production every `${{ secrets.X }}` step fails as unavailable.

## Runs can't be cancelled

* `queue.Postgres.RequestCancel` (`server/queue/postgres.go:545`) has no non-test caller; it's used only in `server/queue/cancel_test.go` and `test/e2e/skeleton_test.go`. The whole cancel path works (doorbell → `CancelJob` on the wire → runner kill → `TerminalizeCancel`), but nothing triggers it: no API, CLI, Slack ([CIC-138](https://linear.app/cicadoci/issue/CIC-138/no-real-slack-integration-on-master-cic-49-socket-mode-events-api-is)) or GitHub hook.
* Rerun exists only through GitHub check_suite/check_run rerequest (`controller.go:483`).

## Audit actions defined but never written

`server/audit/audit.go:27–34` defines approve, cancel, rerun, deploy, rollback, create_run, secret.put and secret.delete. Only `create_run` is ever emitted (`controller.go:887`, via `emitAudit`). The others have no caller (`grep "audit.Action<X>"` finds nothing outside tests). Rerun is recorded as `create_run` with source `github-rerequest`, not `ActionRerun`. Job-token audits (`server/jobtoken/audit.go:41–71`) are written only if `jobtoken.NewManager` is built, and `main.go` doesn't build it.

## Fix

1. API, behind the [CIC-150](https://linear.app/cicadoci/issue/CIC-150/http-api-is-unauthenticated-in-the-shipped-binary-live-job-logs-get) bearer token: `PUT /api/v1/repos/{repo}/secrets/{name}` (write-only, value never returned) and `DELETE` for the same path. List names only, no values. Each writes `secret.put` or `secret.delete` audit rows (org, repo, name, actor; never the value).
2. API: `POST /api/v1/jobs/{id}/cancel` and `POST /api/v1/runs/{id}/cancel` call `RequestCancel` and write `ActionCancel`. Optionally add `POST /api/v1/runs/{id}/rerun` with `ActionRerun`.
3. Thin `cicado secrets set|delete` and `cicado run cancel` CLI subcommands that call these endpoints, so operators don't need curl.
4. e2e: set a secret via the API, run a job that uses it (masked), cancel a running job via the API, and assert the audit rows.

[CIC-93](https://linear.app/cicadoci/issue/CIC-93/secrets-audit-logging) (secrets audit logging, Backlog) and [CIC-48](https://linear.app/cicadoci/issue/CIC-48/screens-secrets-runner-fleet-workflow-viewer-settingstokens) (UI screens) overlap. This ticket is the minimum API and CLI path that makes the MVP usable without a UI.

## Acceptance

On a fresh `make dev`, an operator can set a secret and cancel a running job without touching the database, and both actions show up in `audit_events`.

title: Run-level cancel: POST /api/v1/runs/{id}/cancel, plus optional rerun with ActionRerun
description:
Follow-up to [CIC-194](https://linear.app/cicadoci/issue/CIC-194/no-operator-surface-to-set-secrets-or-cancelrerun-a-run-secretsput-and) (PR [cicadoci/core#143](https://linear.app/cicadoci/review/cic-194-operator-write-surface-secrets-putdelete-job-cancel-audited-637dae6b5767)), which ships job-level cancel only.

**Scope**

* Add `POST /api/v1/runs/{id}/cancel` that cancels every non-terminal job of a run. Needs a jobs-by-run listing in the store, which does not exist yet.
* Optionally add rerun (`ActionRerun` audit event).
* Same rules as [CIC-194](https://linear.app/cicadoci/issue/CIC-194/no-operator-surface-to-set-secrets-or-cancelrerun-a-run-secretsput-and): behind the existing auth + audit chain, fail-closed, no raw database errors to the client, audit row only when something actually changed (unknown or finished run must not write a false `ActionCancel` row).
* CLI: `cicado run cancel <runID>`.

**Out of scope for** [cicadoci/core#143](https://linear.app/cicadoci/review/cic-194-operator-write-surface-secrets-putdelete-job-cancel-audited-637dae6b5767) (Dwight review, 2026-10-06).
